title: Overpacking Is Travelers' Biggest Mistake
paragraphs: You're packing for a trip. You've already put the essentials in: clothes, shoes, toiletries, a charger. But then you start thinking. What if it rains? What if it gets colder than you thought? Maybe you need another pair of shoes — and your warmer jacket, just in case.
Before long, your suitcase is full of things you might not even need.
If this sounds like you, you're not alone. A new survey from travel assistance company Global Rescue found that overpacking is the most common mistake named by travelers.

Thirty-eight percent of those who were surveyed said packing too much was their biggest travel mistake. That's up from 32% in 2025, but still much better than it was before the COVID-19 pandemic. In February 2020, 74% named overpacking as their biggest mistake.

Dan Richards, CEO of Global Rescue, said overpacking is a problem the company sees year after year. Richards said that the extra weight caused by overpacking can create stress when people should be enjoying the freedom of their trip.
Richards also said that overpacking can lead to injuries and make it harder to move quickly in an emergency.
Other common mistakes travelers named included leaving too little time between flights (19%), having a very busy itinerary (10%) and forgetting to save maps or travel details for offline use (8%).
The survey also asked travelers about their favorite travel hacks.
The most popular was putting a smart tag in checked luggage, chosen by 31% of travelers. Another 16% said they email themselves digital copies of important documents.
To fit more into a suitcase, 10% use space-saving packing bags, while another 10% roll their clothes instead of folding them.
If only there was a hack for knowing what you don't need to pack!
